findings.title: Legacy SQL path fails as invalid SQL and error-logs every query
findings.body: The explicit reject added in ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery does not cover the frontend entry point. UnmarshalSQLCommand always calls NewSQLCommand, and NewSQLCommand still calls sql.TablesList for every non-empty expression. reader.go itself notes that ExpressionQueryReader has not replaced the existing parser, so this is the path dashboard and alert evaluation use. TablesList now always fails because the stub RunCommands returns an error, and that failure is mapped to a BadRequest whose public message is "error reading SQL command" (lines 33-35). That text is wrong: the statement was not parsed or rejected as invalid SQL; the DuckDB engine was removed to close the RCE/LFI issue. Before returning, TablesList logs the raw expression and the assembled SELECT json_serialize_sql(...) command at Error (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:28), and NewSQLCommand logs the raw SQL again at Warn (line 32). Instances that had enabled SQL expressions will therefore show a misleading invalid-query error and emit error-level logs containing the expression text on every panel refresh and every alert evaluation. Reject the feature in NewSQLCommand/UnmarshalSQLCommand before calling TablesList, with a stable disabled-feature error, and do not log the statement at Error.

findings.title: SQL gate is an inverted no-op that can panic and misreports the feature
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions is the only explicit SQL-expression gate, but it is not a real flag check. It sets enabled to the negation of FlagSqlExpressions and then returns false from both branches, so the flag cannot turn the feature back on. That matches the security intent, but it hides the kill switch, and the error returned to callers (line 131) is "sqlExpressions is not implemented", which is false — the feature existed and is being disabled because of the RCE/LFI vulnerability. The flag read also panics if ExpressionQueryReader.features is nil. This case did not touch features before, so a reader built without toggles now crashes on SQL queries instead of returning a controlled error. Return false without reading the flag, and use an error that says SQL expressions are disabled.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions stay disabled
findings.body: This change set is the in-tree fix for the SQL-expression RCE/LFI issue, but it adds or updates no tests. Nothing asserts that ReadQuery rejects SQL queries even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled, that UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand fail closed without executing a statement, or that DB.RunCommands and DB.QueryFramesInto do not run SQL or touch the filesystem. The disable is an always-false helper with inverted flag logic plus stub methods that return "not implemented". Restoring a DuckDB call inside RunCommands, or changing the helper so the feature flag reaches NewSQLCommand while a later DB implementation executes queries, would not fail CI. Add a regression test for both entry points that expects a disabled-feature error with the flag on and asserts the supplied statement is not executed.
